A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial benchmark revision and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark-distribution analyses, model re-evaluations, CQD-Hybrid experiments, and results on three proposed benchmarks, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical analyses and reports additional QTO comparisons, negation experiments, and evaluations of the revised benchmarks.

M1.justification: The documented CQD-Hybrid solver is unchanged: observed triples receive score 1, predicted scores are normalized to [0, 0.9], and inference uses the same capped CQD beam search. Negation evaluation does not establish a new solver component; benchmark sampling changes are addressed under E3.

E1.justification: V1 explicitly excludes negation, whereas v2 evaluates five negated-query types on the original benchmarks and all three +H benchmarks (Tables A.1–A.2 and D.5). The underlying KGs and the 4p/4i query types were already present in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds QTO to the original-benchmark comparisons and revised +H evaluations. CQD-Hybrid also joins the +H comparisons, from which v1 explicitly excluded it. The four existing neural comparators remain; FIT is discussed but explicitly not separately evaluated.

E3.justification: The +H evaluation design changes from full-inference-only sampling, generally 50,000 pairs per query type and 10,000 for 4p/4i, to 10,000 pairs per reducibility/full-inference stratum. For example, v2 specifies 30,000 balanced 3p pairs. The published KG split counts, temporal splitting procedure, and existing model hyperparameters remain largely unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds diagnostics testing whether known-link effects extend to negation, stratifying positive reasoning trees and associated performance (Appendix A.1 and Tables A.2/D.5). Tables D.2–D.4 add stratified analyses of the revised benchmarks, while Figures D.1–D.2 extend the earlier full-inference-only cardinality analyses to partial/full comparisons. The original-benchmark cardinality plots are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report MRR point estimates and descriptive frequencies without run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance procedures.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the +H result tables under revised sampling and adds QTO, negation, and stratified result entries. For example, CQD's FB15k237+H 2i MRR changes from 18.4 in v1 Table 5 to 11.3 in v2 Table 4; this is not a same-setting performance loss. Some retained original-benchmark entries also change, including NELL995 CQD 2u1p overall MRR from 16.0 to 14.6 (v1 Table A.2; v2 Table A.5).

T1.justification: V2 defines positive and negative reasoning-tree components and adds formal negated-query definitions, including a De Morgan derivation (Appendices A.1/B). Equation 1 also corrects the displayed MRR formula by adding the missing reciprocal of rank. The original hardness definitions and 4p/4i formulas are retained, with the latter relocated.

C1.justification: The proposed benchmark contribution changes from exclusively irreducible queries to balanced coverage of partial- and full-inference queries. CQD-Hybrid is recast from a novel, SoTA-surpassing hybrid model to a simple diagnostic extension competitive with existing methods. The overarching critique of inflated benchmark performance remains.

C2.justification: V1 accepts the old benchmarks for stratified hybrid evaluation; v2 discourages their use for both hybrid and neural solvers and emphasizes balanced hardness coverage. V2 adds arguments about arbitrary triple-independence and split-ratio assumptions, interprets model rankings as possible overfitting to easy queries, and qualifies that negative-tree effects depend on each model's treatment of negation.

D1.justification: V1 promises code and benchmark release upon acceptance; v2 Appendix F supplies a repository access link for benchmarks, generation scripts, and CQD-Hybrid. Appendix G.2 newly documents training-query construction, quota enforcement, answer truncation, and random subsampling. Existing solver hyperparameters are mostly retained. Repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: V1 claims that explicitly retrieving training links in a hybrid CQA solver is unprecedented. V2 acknowledges QTO and FIT as prior hybrid solvers, describes CQD-Hybrid as inspired by them, and distinguishes its minimal modification from their calibration and inference machinery. This substantially revises the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, research questions, takeaways, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around a spectrum of hardness and balanced evaluation. The standalone hybrid-solver subsection is integrated into Section 5, related work moves to Appendix C, and four-link query formulas move to Appendix E within a reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text to two columns, replaces the large main-text Table 2 with a selected excerpt, and relocates v1 Table 4 to Appendix A.3. It adds a negation-structure diagram and several stratified tables. Figure 3 is redrawn for the revised benchmarks and displays QTO instead of GNN-QE, which remains evaluated in tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves prior-work attribution, comparator coverage, negation evidence, and reproducibility documentation. However, the central shift from full-inference-only to balanced benchmarks leaves an important aggregation question unresolved: equal QA-pair quotas do not establish balanced weighting under the query-averaged MRR formula, and Table D.2 does not reconcile these weights. V2 also retains the claim that ICEWS18+H is harder across all query types despite contrary aggregate results in Table 4, such as GNN-QE 3i MRR of 26.5 versus 8.8 and 13.3 on the other +H datasets. These gains and unresolved problems in the revised contribution prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
